title: Ind AS 38 "Intangible Assets"
outcomes: Apply the definition and recognition criteria for intangibles.
Measure separately acquired and combination-acquired intangibles.
Distinguish research and development and apply capitalisation criteria.
Apply cost/revaluation models, useful lives and amortisation.

meta.exam_tip: For R&D questions, find the date all six criteria are met — costs before it are expensed forever.

concepts.title: Definition: identifiability, control and future benefits
body: Ind AS 38 treats as an intangible asset any non-monetary resource that has no physical form yet can be identified. Identifiable means either separable (can be sold, licensed, rented or exchanged) or arising from contractual or other legal rights.
Control is the power to obtain the benefits and restrict others' access — usually through legal rights. Skilled staff, market share or customer loyalty without contracts usually lack control.
Future economic benefits include revenues and cost savings. Where an item has both tangible and intangible parts, judgement decides which dominates (e.g. software integral to a machine is PPE).
concepts.analogy: Intangibles are rights you can point to and protect — not general goodwill or talent.
concepts.work: A trained workforce is valuable but not an asset, as employees can leave.

concepts.title: Acquired intangibles: separately and in business combinations
body: Recognition requires probable future benefits and reliably measurable cost. For separately acquired intangibles, both are presumed met; cost is purchase price plus non-refundable taxes and directly attributable costs (professional fees, testing), excluding introduction costs, advertising and administrative overheads.

In a business combination, intangibles are recognised at fair value separately from goodwill if identifiable — even if the acquiree had not recognised them (e.g. customer relationships, brands, in-process R&D).
Acquisition by Government grant may be at fair value or nominal amount plus directly attributable costs; exchanges follow fair value unless commercial substance is lacking.
concepts.analogy: Buying an intangible proves its value; building one internally needs stricter tests.
concepts.work: An acquired brand appears in consolidated accounts even though the target never showed it.

concepts.title: Internally generated intangibles: research and development
body: Internally generated goodwill is never recognised. Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists and similar items are not recognised.

For internal projects, research phase spending is expensed. Development spending is capitalised only when all of these are shown: technical feasibility of completion; intention to complete and use or sell; ability to use or sell; how the asset will generate probable future benefits (a market or internal usefulness); availability of technical, financial and other resources; and ability to measure the expenditure reliably.

If research and development phases cannot be distinguished, all costs are treated as research. Costs expensed earlier are not reinstated later. Cost includes materials, services, employee costs and directly attributable overheads from the date criteria are met; it excludes selling, admin and training costs and initial operating losses.
concepts.analogy: Research is always expensed; development waits until success is demonstrable.
concepts.work: Designing a prototype after feasibility is proven is development; exploring alternative materials is research.

concepts.title: Measurement after recognition, useful life and amortisation
body: After recognition: cost model, or revaluation model only if fair value can be measured by reference to an active market (rare for intangibles). Revaluation follows principles like Ind AS 16.

Useful life is finite (amortised systematically from availability for use, over the shorter of economic and legal life) or indefinite (no foreseeable limit to cash flows; not amortised, tested annually for impairment and reviewed each period). Residual value is normally zero unless there is a commitment or active market.

Amortisation reflects the pattern of consumption; a revenue-based method is presumed inappropriate except where the asset is expressed as a measure of revenue or revenue and consumption are highly correlated. Life, method and residual value are reviewed at least each year end. Derecognition gains or losses go to profit or loss.
concepts.analogy: Finite lives are amortised; indefinite lives are tested for impairment instead.
concepts.work: A broadcasting licence renewable at little cost may have an indefinite life.

illustrations.title: A new drug formulation
illustrations.q: Nova Pharma spends ₹40 lakh on research (April–July). On 1 August all six development criteria are first met. Development costs are ₹20 lakh in July and ₹70 lakh from August to March. The formulation is available for use on 1 October of the next year (expected life 5 years, straight-line). How much is expensed and capitalised in the first year, and what is the amortisation for the following year?

head: Item
Treatment
₹ lakh
rows: Capitalise as intangible asset under development
Amortisation next year (6 months from 1 October)
solution.title: Ind AS 38 — R&D

checks.label: Expensed (₹ lakh): research + development before criteria met
Amortisation for the first year of use (₹ lakh)

illustrations.title: Recognise or not?
illustrations.q: Decide recognition: (a) a customer list bought from a competitor for ₹5 crore; (b) the company's own brand built through years of advertising; (c) a 3-year software licence purchased; (d) ₹2 crore spent training sales staff; (e) a customer relationship of an acquired subsidiary, valued at ₹8 crore in a business combination; (f) costs of launching a new product line.

Recognise?
Reason
rows: Separately acquired; price reflects expected benefits
Internally generated brands cannot be recognised
Acquired right with reliable cost; amortise over 3 years
Identifiable intangible acquired in a business combination at fair value, separate from goodwill

solution.title: Recognition

jobs.title: Capitalising software development
jobs.situation: A tech company capitalised all salaries of its developers for the year.
steps: Identify the date each project met all six criteria.
Expense costs before that date and research costs.
Check amortisation start and impairment of incomplete projects.
jobs.takeaway: The capitalisation start date is the heart of an R&D review.

mcqs.q: An asset is identifiable if it:
options: Is separable or arises from contractual or legal rights
mcqs.explain: Either test is enough. In practice: licences arise from legal rights.
mcqs.topic: Definition: identifiability, control and future benefits

mcqs.explain: Costs cannot be distinguished from developing the business as a whole. In practice: acquired brands are recognised.
mcqs.topic: Internally generated intangibles: research and development

mcqs.explain: No asset can be shown to exist in research. In practice: track phases separately.
mcqs.topic: Internally generated intangibles: research and development

mcqs.q: Development costs expensed in earlier periods can later be:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 38 prohibits reinstatement. In practice: capitalise from the criteria date only.
mcqs.topic: Internally generated intangibles: research and development

mcqs.q: An intangible with an indefinite useful life is:
options: Not amortised but tested for impairment annually
mcqs.explain: Indefinite does not mean infinite; life is reviewed each period. In practice: change to finite is an estimate change.
mcqs.topic: Measurement after recognition, useful life and amortisation

mcqs.q: The revaluation model for intangibles requires:
mcqs.explain: Without an active market, the cost model applies. In practice: taxi licences may have one.
mcqs.topic: Measurement after recognition, useful life and amortisation

mcqs.q: Customer relationships of an acquired company are recognised in consolidation:
options: At fair value, separately from goodwill, if identifiable
Only if the acquiree recognised them
mcqs.explain: Business combination accounting captures identifiable intangibles. In practice: valuation experts are used.
mcqs.topic: Acquired intangibles: separately and in business combinations

options: Presumed inappropriate, rebuttable in limited cases
mcqs.explain: Revenue reflects more than consumption of the asset. In practice: allowed when the right is expressed as a revenue cap.
mcqs.topic: Measurement after recognition, useful life and amortisation

model.title: Recognition

summary: Identifiable (separable or legal), controlled, future benefits.
Acquired: cost or fair value in a combination.
Research → expense; development → capitalise after six criteria.
No internally generated goodwill, brands, customer lists.
Finite: amortise; indefinite: annual impairment test.
traps: Expensed development costs are never reinstated.

viva.model: A non-monetary resource with no physical form that is identifiable, controlled by the entity and expected to yield future economic benefits.
Technical feasibility, intention to complete, ability to use or sell, probable benefits, availability of resources, and reliable measurement of cost.

viva.q: Why is internally generated goodwill not recognised?
viva.model: Goodwill built internally fails the identifiability test, and its cost cannot be measured reliably.

viva.q: How is an indefinite-life intangible treated?
viva.model: It is not amortised; it is tested for impairment every year and its life assessment is reviewed each period.

viva.q: What is the effect of failing to separate research from development?
viva.model: All the expenditure is treated as research and expensed.

cases.title: PixelSoft Ltd.
cases.case: PixelSoft Ltd. develops a game engine. Feasibility was proven on 1 September; costs before that were ₹1.2 crore, and after, ₹3 crore including ₹20 lakh of marketing launch expenses. It also bought a 10-year music licence for ₹50 lakh and a domain name renewable indefinitely at minimal cost.

mcqs.q: Amount capitalised for the game engine (₹ crore):
mcqs.explain: Post-criteria costs of 3.0 less marketing 0.2 = 2.8. In practice: pre-September costs are expensed.
mcqs.topic: Internally generated intangibles: research and development

mcqs.q: The ₹1.2 crore spent before 1 September is:
mcqs.explain: Costs before criteria are met are expensed and never reinstated. In practice: keep project logs.
mcqs.topic: Internally generated intangibles: research and development

mcqs.q: Annual amortisation of the music licence (₹ lakh):
mcqs.explain: 50 ÷ 10 = 5, over its legal life. In practice: start when available for use.
mcqs.topic: Measurement after recognition, useful life and amortisation

mcqs.q: The domain name renewable indefinitely at minimal cost may be:
options: An indefinite-life intangible tested annually for impairment
mcqs.explain: No foreseeable limit to its cash flows if renewals are expected. In practice: review each year.
mcqs.topic: Measurement after recognition, useful life and amortisation
